nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori proposed the 'magic wavelength' optical lattice clock, in which neutral atoms are trapped so that the trap light shifts the upper and lower clock states by the same amount. This lets thousands of atoms be interrogated at once without perturbing the clock transition. Katori demonstrated the first such clocks with strontium. Ye turned the concept into a metrology tool of record-breaking stability and accuracy, reaching fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and beyond. He did this by combining ultrastable lasers, femtosecond frequency combs and control over atomic many-body interactions. These clocks now outperform the caesium standard by more than two orders of magnitude and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. They resolve gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences and enable searches for dark matter and for variation of fundamental constants. Their work turned optical frequency measurement into community infrastructure and opened new ways to test fundamental physics.
